about.summary: I'm completing a Bachelor of Software Engineering at FPT University, Can Tho. I've worked across the software development lifecycle in a company team at Rikkeisoft, in group projects, and on AnSite, a capstone project I helped take from idea to deployment. I adapt quickly to new stacks and domains, from .NET and Node.js to Python and mobile integration, and I use AI coding agents with a disciplined workflow: plan first, review every change, test before merge. The projects below show the details.
feat.ansite.title: AnSite: Camera-Based Safety Platform for Factories
feat.ansite.meta: Backend Developer | Capstone Project | NestJS, PostgreSQL, Socket.IO, Docker, Python
feat.ansite.b1: Split the system by workload because raw video is bandwidth-heavy: a Python edge agent on the factory LAN handles camera streams and YOLO/VLM detection, while a NestJS cloud API centralizes database access, keeping AI processing isolated from the dashboard.
feat.ansite.b2: Fixed a lock-scope bug in the camera worker: the lock was held across slow frame processing and uploads, blocking live config updates for about 71 s; narrowing the critical section brought updates to 191-361 ms, with a regression test.
feat.ansite.b3: Implemented the NestJS alert ingestion API with idempotent writes (a retry with the same event ID and body returns the existing alert instead of creating a duplicate), composite PostgreSQL indexes for organization-scoped queries, and real-time updates through Socket.IO rooms.
feat.ansite.b4: Implemented per-device activation and SHA-256-hashed device credentials with constant-time comparison.
feat.ansite.b5: Deployed the NestJS API to a Linux VPS with Docker Compose and Caddy, with GitHub Actions CI for API, web and edge and a migration replay gate on a fresh PostgreSQL database.
feat.ansite.b6: Documented and enforced an AI-assisted delivery workflow: versioned AGENTS.md rules, plan-first changes with per-phase acceptance criteria, planner/executor separation, and an independent diff/CI audit before merge.
feat.eh.title: EventHub: Event Booking Platform
feat.eh.meta: Backend Developer | Personal Project | ASP.NET Core 8, SQL Server, Ocelot, SignalR
feat.eh.b1: Built an event booking system with 10 ASP.NET Core services backed by 9 SQL Server databases, behind an Ocelot gateway that routes REST and SignalR traffic and forwards JWT tokens to protected services.
feat.eh.b2: Implemented a booking flow that validates tickets and vouchers, takes VNPay/MoMo payment, and calls compensating actions to restore tickets and vouchers when payment fails, instead of a distributed transaction across service databases.
feat.cs.title: Calendar Shop: Mobile E-Commerce App
feat.cs.meta: Backend Developer | Team of 5 | ASP.NET Core 8, SQL Server, OData, VNPay
feat.cs.b1: Implemented the VNPay payment flow with callback signature, amount and order-state checks before confirming payment, plus a background worker that cancels orders left unpaid after a 15-minute timeout.
feat.cs.b2: Chose OData over per-screen endpoints so the mobile app could filter, page and select fields without new endpoints; order queries use EF Core projection to avoid loading full entities.
feat.cs.b3: Implemented server-side refresh-token rotation with revocation on logout, password change/reset and account lock, used by the Flutter app for silent re-login.
exp.meta: Rikkeisoft | Ho Chi Minh City | VMS (Visitor & Manpower Management System)
exp.b1: Implemented cache-stampede protection in a shared Redis caching package adopted by 4 NestJS services: a token-checked distributed lock lets only one request rebuild an expired entry while the rest back off with jitter, instead of a local lock that would not coordinate across service instances.
exp.b2: Implemented version-based cache invalidation (one Redis counter per entity, hashed query keys), so a write makes the entity's older cache keys unreachable, instead of scanning and deleting every query variant; traced and fixed a bug where one write bumped the version several times and invalidated cached entries too often.

journey.heading: My Journey
j1.title: Where my passion for technology began: level design for a player community
j1.text: From 2014 to 2018 I designed nearly 100 custom levels for the 2D platformer Plazma Burst 2, more than 30 of them highly rated by the community. Players came to me with their own requests, so I gathered their feedback, built each level around what they wanted and kept refining it. I became one of the game's best-known level designers and was invited to lead one of its largest player clans: my first experience of working directly with users and a community.
j2.title: Pre-university academic awards
j2.text: I took part in academic and English competitions through middle and high school, and ranked among the top 10 students every semester.

j3.text: I began the Software Engineering program at FPT University, Can Tho.
j4.title: English Edu-Tourism Program, UniKL MIIT

j5.title: Completed Vovinam martial arts training
j5.text: I finished the full 3-term Vovinam course, six months in total, which built my discipline and physical resilience.
j6.title: Joined FEL — FPTU Can Tho English Club
j6.text: I joined FPTU Can Tho's English Club and took an active part in its events, which strengthened my English, communication and teamwork, and later led me to build the club's website.
j7.title: Top 5, Engineering & Technology Faculty Group
j7.text: I was ranked top 5 in the Engineering & Technology Faculty Group in Fall 2024. Seven merit certificates followed from 2024 to 2026: three Excellent and four Honorable Student of Trimester.

j8.title: Arduino autonomous robot project
j8.text: With a friend, I designed and built a path-following, dust-collecting robot using Arduino. We completed it within one month.
j9.title: FEL Club website
j9.text: I built a static frontend site for FEL Club that loads its event data from a JSON file, deployed on GitHub Pages.
j10.title: OJT at Rikkeisoft (VMS project)
j10.text: I interned at Rikkeisoft HCM on the VMS project: a shared Redis caching library for four NestJS services, and the User Management feature, built end to end.
j11.title: AnSite as my capstone project
j11.text: I started AnSite as my capstone project, inspired by my OJT work on VMS at Rikkeisoft: an AI vision platform that turns factory CCTV into safety alerts.
j12.title: Completing my degree (expected)
j12.text: I expect to complete the Software Engineering program at FPT University, Can Tho in December 2026; the official graduation ceremony is held in July 2027.
